claim: A run executes exactly one improvement; a run that executes no candidate ends with an interrupt report and no changes.
Candidate priority order: (1) make test failure, (2) source TODO/FIXME, (3) README/docs vs implementation mismatch; pick the first suitable one.
Run output is minimal change + verification + one commit; the run never pushes (harness lands the chain result); deploy, release and external transmission are forbidden.

Forbidden in a run: push/force-push/history rewrite/tag and release ops/deploy, reading or committing secrets, calling production APIs, starting a second improvement, major dependency updates, breaking refactors, editing out-of-scope repos.
A run targets 15-30 minutes; work that would exceed it must be split, implementing only the first slice and recording the rest as remaining tasks for the next run.
Never commit while existing tests are broken; fix them or revert the change.
The verification step of a run is `make test`.
Makefile defines `make test` and `make test-unit` as `pytest tests-unit -v` (unit only); `test-all` additionally runs integration `tests/`, which launch a real server.
tests-unit/ holds 61 test files, measured 918 passed / 1 failed / 10 skipped in ~30s on 2026-09-20; one known red test is hidden by continue-on-error in test-unit.yml CI.

Core ComfyUI must not add uploads, telemetry, analytics, tracking, usage reporting, crash reporting, update checks, remote config, feature flags or any outbound internet request path; model downloading is allowed only when explicitly user-initiated, limited to the requested artifact, without telemetry.
Opt-in, opt-out, anonymized, aggregated, diagnostic or user-triggered labels do not make an internet request path acceptable; local-only behavior is allowed when it stays on the user's machine.
Fixes must touch the narrowest code path that explains the bug or behavior; change the least amount of files possible; broad multi-file changes are presumed bad unless the scope is directly required.
Prefer practical fixes over broad architecture work; do not add new dependencies unless absolutely necessary; add abstractions only when they remove real repeated logic.
Delete obsolete code aggressively when newer infrastructure makes it useless: dead fallbacks, migration paths, unused options, debug prints, unreachable branches.
ComfyUI is described as 'the most powerful and modular AI engine for content creation'; this repository is a local fork of it used for image-generation research.
Nodes follow the conventions INPUT_TYPES, RETURN_TYPES, FUNCTION, CATEGORY and register through the local NODE_CLASS_MAPPINGS mapping; nodes.py mappings are referenced from all layers.
Node-level code must not patch model code directly; any node behavior that modifies model behavior must go through the model patcher class.

Model implementations must use an existing optimized Comfy Kitchen or ComfyUI operation when it supports the required math and layout; a local implementation is allowed only when no existing optimized operation supports the contract.
This repository is a fork of upstream ComfyUI about 515 commits ahead, of which about 20 are fork-specific (git log measured 2026-09-26); the bulk of the lead is upstream merge commits.

Subset runs (`pytest tests-unit/assets_test ...`) register the option as an initial conftest, which is why standalone runs were green.
